target: A sealed lot contains exactly 500 firmware-programmed devices. Inspectors sample 60 devices uniformly without replacement and find zero boot failures. Acceptance requires 95% confidence that no more than 2% of the lot (10 devices) are defective. The lot cannot be resampled, and the team must decide whether this zero-failure sample alone certifies the acceptance limit.
surface: A previous firmware-device lot passed after a 60-device sample showed zero boot failures. Its dashboard treated the observed 0/60 defect rate as the lot defect rate and accepted because 0% was below the 2% limit.
structural: An archaeological survey sampled n sites uniformly without replacement from a finite set of N sites and found zero sites containing an artifact. If K sites in the full set contained artifacts, the exact probability of seeing zero was C(N-K,n)/C(N,n). To form a one-sided 95% upper bound on K, analysts found the largest K for which that zero-result probability remained at least 0.05, then compared K/N with the required ceiling.
rubric: Explicitly selects the exact finite-population hypergeometric zero-event bound rather than 0/60 or an infinite-population shortcut alone.
Finds K=22 remains above the cutoff (about 0.0563) while K=23 is below it (about 0.0492), giving an upper bound around 22-23 devices.
Concludes the sample does not certify at most 10 defective devices (2%) and rejects acceptance on this evidence.
Notes uniform sampling without replacement and the one-sided confidence interpretation.
